  requires forall i,i',j::0<=i<i'<a.Length0 && 0<=j<a.Length1 ==> a[i,j]<=a[i',j]
  requires exists i,j :: 0<=i<a.Length0 && 0<=j<a.Length1 && a[i,j]==key
  ensures 0<=m<a.Length0 && 0<=n<a.Length1
  ensures a[m,n]==key
{
  m,n:=0, a.Length1-1;
  while a[m,n] !=key
    invariant 0<=m<a.Length0 && 0<=n<a.Length1
    invariant exists i,j :: m<=i<a.Length0 && 0<=j<=n && a[i,j]==key
    decreases a.Length0-m+n

    if a[m,n] < key {
      m:=m+1;

    }
  }
}

raw_response: {"spec_element": "requires", "proof_obligation": "preservation", "diagnosis": "The row-sortedness precondition bounds j' by a.Length1 - 1 instead of a.Length1, so it says nothing about the last column. The loop starts at n = a.Length1-1. When a[m,n] < key, the body does m := m+1. To keep the invariant 'exists i,j :: m<=i && j<=n && a[i,j]==key', it must rule out the key lying in row m at some column j <= n. That needs a[m,j] <= a[m,n] for j < n = a.Length1-1, which the weakened precondition does not give. Without it the existential witness can be lost. The bounds invariant 0<=n can then also fail, because n may be decremented past 0.", "repair": "requires forall i,j,j'::0<=i<a.Length0 && 0<=j<j'<a.Length1 ==> a[i,j]<=a[i,j']"}
reasoning_content: I'm spotting a bug: the precondition only requires j<j'<a.Length1-1, missing coverage of the last column, so row sortedness doesn't fully hold. This makes me question whether the invariant at n>=0 can actually be preserved when a[m,n] > key, since decrementing n could go out of bounds if key's position isn't properly constrained.
